questions.q: How does AWS describe the fundamental split in the Shared Responsibility Model?
options: AWS is responsible for security of the cloud; the customer is responsible for security in the cloud
AWS is responsible for all security, with no customer obligations whatsoever
The customer is responsible for all security, including the physical data centers
Security responsibility is decided case by case with no general rule
questions.explain: This exact split — of the cloud vs. in the cloud — is the model's core statement.

questions.q: Which of the following is squarely AWS's responsibility under the model?
options: Physical data center security, hardware, the host operating system, and the global network infrastructure
Whether a customer's S3 bucket is configured to be publicly readable
The IAM policies a customer attaches to their own users
Whether a customer's data is encrypted at rest
questions.explain: The physical and infrastructure layer underneath what customers configure is AWS's job — everything the customer configures is the customer's job.

questions.q: How does the responsibility line differ between EC2 and RDS?
options: On EC2, the customer patches the guest OS; on RDS, AWS patches the underlying database engine while the customer still manages IAM and backups
There is no difference — both services split responsibility identically
On RDS, AWS manages the customer's IAM policies for them automatically
On EC2, AWS manages 100% of the OS and the customer manages nothing
questions.explain: The line moves depending on how much AWS manages for a given service — RDS shifts OS/engine patching onto AWS, EC2 does not.

questions.q: Why is a publicly readable, misconfigured S3 bucket considered the customer's responsibility rather than AWS's?
options: Bucket policies and public-access settings fall on the customer's side of the line ('security in the cloud'), even though AWS secures the underlying S3 infrastructure
Because AWS does not actually offer any security controls for S3 buckets
Because S3 has no shared responsibility split at all
Because only paid AWS Support customers are responsible for bucket configuration
questions.explain: AWS secures S3's infrastructure, but bucket policy and access configuration are explicitly the customer's job.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the most common real-world category of AWS security incident?
options: Customer-side misconfiguration, such as an overly permissive IAM policy or a publicly exposed S3 bucket
AWS's physical data centers being breached
Failures in AWS's global network backbone
AWS's hypervisor being compromised
questions.explain: The lesson identifies customer-side misconfiguration, not AWS infrastructure failure, as the most common real incident category.
